Package com.j3d.engine.scene.nodes.layer

Class Layer

java.lang.Object
java.util.AbstractCollection<Thing>
java.util.AbstractList<Thing>
java.util.ArrayList<Thing>
com.j3d.engine.scene.nodes.layer.Layer
All Implemented Interfaces:
SceneObjectList, SceneObject, HasProperties, Serializable, Cloneable, Iterable<Thing>, Collection<Thing>, List<Thing>, RandomAccess, SequencedCollection<Thing>
public class Layer extends ArrayList<Thing> implements SceneObjectList
A Layer is a fundamental concept in the rendering pipeline, representing a collection of Thing instances that are rendered together. The SceneManager processes these layers in a specific order, drawing the contents of each layer to the screen.

The Layer class extends ArrayList, providing a way to manage the objects within it. You can add, remove, and reorder objects in a layer to dynamically change the scene's composition.

  • Layers allow you to group related Things, making it easier to manage complex scenes.

    • invokeSwingHooks

      public void invokeSwingHooks()
      Description copied from interface: SceneObjectList
      A method to initialise anything swing related within the constructor. This is typically called within the SceneObjectList's constructor who needs to create an object outside the EDT thread.

      A use case (the current use case) would be when an SceneObjectList is loaded from disk to memory and the Spinner dialog is blocking the EDT thread. After the throbber has finished, you may call invokeSwingHooks safely rather than fighting with a blocked EDT thread.

      Specified by:
      invokeSwingHooks in interface SceneObjectList

    • draw

      public void draw(Graphics2D graphics2D)
      Draws all Thing instances in this layer using the provided Graphics2D context. The drawing order is determined by the distance of each Thing's centroid from the camera position, ensuring proper depth representation in the rendered scene.
      Parameters:
      graphics2D - The Graphics2D context used for drawing.

    • instantDelete

      public void instantDelete()
      Description copied from interface: SceneObjectList
      An internal delete method which all implementors should override for instantaneous deletion.

      This method should not be called by a user interface things. However, any object overriding the method must provide a way to delete everything relating to it.

      Specified by:

    • deleteLater

      public DirtyVoidAction deleteLater()
      Description copied from interface: SceneObjectList
      Deletes the object.

      The use of the word "later" is because the action of deletion is only ever done once the Action object is out of the history's bounds. At that point CleanableAction.cleanup() is called, which actually deletes.

      Specified by:
      deleteLater in interface SceneObjectList
      Returns:
